string.text: A new PDA encyclopedia article is available: Life Before the Accident.

There are five stash tiers in the Zone: green, cyan, purple, legendary (orange), and red. The higher the tier, the more valuable its possible contents and the harder it is to find. 

%c[255,170,220,255]How many stashes exist%c[default] 
At the start of a new game, the system selects 400 stashes from 1,236 prepared locations: 

%c[255,130,220,120]• 240 green;%c[default] 
%c[255,100,205,235]• 80 cyan;%c[default] 
%c[255,190,140,230]• 40 purple;%c[default] 
%c[255,255,170,80]• 20 legendary;%c[default] 
%c[255,235,105,90]• 20 red.%c[default] 

The starting 400 are not a permanent system limit. If a new lead has no suitable hidden stash of the required tier, the system can create another stash at an unused prepared location. The total number of stashes can therefore grow beyond 400. 

A fully looted stash is not gone forever. Once the player moves far enough away, it receives a new location and new contents. 

%c[255,170,220,255]Where to look%c[default] 
Stashes occupy prepared locations inside buildings, near furniture, machinery and vehicles, in recesses, under stairs, and among ordinary clutter. 

If the marker is present but the container is not visible, check: 

• another floor, the roof, or the basement; 
• inside and behind furniture; 
• a vehicle's bed, interior, and underside; 
• recesses, corners, and objects directly around the marker's center. 

%c[255,170,220,255]Searching without equipment%c[default] 
Some stashes can be discovered by approaching them: 

%c[255,130,220,120]• green — within 10 meters;%c[default] 
%c[255,100,205,235]• cyan — within 5 meters;%c[default] 
%c[255,190,140,230]• purple — within 3 meters;%c[default] 
%c[255,255,170,80]• legendary — only from a lead or with the Magnet;%c[default] 
%c[255,235,105,90]• red — only from a lead.%c[default] 

Once discovered, the container receives a permanent PDA marker. 

%c[255,170,220,255]Stash-search equipment%c[default] 
Regular artefact detectors do not search for stashes. Use the special black-and-white Homemade, Wave, and Magnet detectors instead. Equip the device in the detector slot and keep it active. Its signal pulses faster as the stash gets closer. 

Signal range depends on the model:

• Homemade: green — 20 m, cyan — 10 m.
• Wave: cyan — 15 m, purple — 10 m.
• Magnet: cyan — 20 m, purple — 15 m, legendary — 5 m.

The Homemade and Wave only provide a sound signal. The Magnet also reveals a permanent legendary stash marker within 5 m. None of these devices detects red stashes.

The devices consume charge only while active. A Krona Battery adds 15 minutes of operation, up to full capacity. 

The first three newly discovered purple stashes introduce the system: 

1. The first contains the Homemade detector. 
2. The second contains a radio beacon and USB-1 software. 
3. The third contains three working Stalker PDAs. 

After the Homemade, new purple, legendary, and red stashes can yield the Wave, then the Magnet. Each model has protection against a long run of bad luck. Once the Magnet is obtained, detectors continue to appear as random stash loot. Selling or losing a device does not restart the sequence.

The starting Metal Detector opens the normal inventory window of the nearest accessible stash within 3 m when the container is difficult to reach manually. Take items with the usual controls, including Take All. Green, cyan, and purple stashes do not need to be discovered first; legendary and red stashes must already be revealed. The action is unavailable while another stash window is open. 

%c[255,170,220,255]Sources of stash leads%c[default] 
A lead immediately adds an exact colored marker to the PDA. There are several ways to obtain one. 

%c[255,255,190,90]1. Looting other stashes%c[default] 

• A cyan stash: 9% for a purple lead and 1% for a red lead. 
• A purple stash: 12% for a legendary lead and 5% for a red lead. 
• A legendary stash: 25% for a red lead. 

%c[255,255,190,90]2. PDAs carried by dead stalkers%c[default] 
Ordinary corpses do not reveal coordinates automatically. You must find and hack a physical PDA on the body. Such PDAs can also appear inside stashes. 

Hacking requires installed USB software: 

• Novice PDA + USB-1 → green stash; 
• Stalker PDA + USB-1 → cyan stash; 
• Veteran PDA + USB-2 → purple stash; 
• Master PDA + USB-3 → guaranteed legendary stash. 

During a hack, traces can reveal additional purple, legendary, and red coordinates. Weakening protection raises the chance of an unattempted trace. Each trace tier allows one attempt; its reward is granted after the hack succeeds. Reloading alone does not reroll a particular PDA. 

A failed attempt or manually leaving the hack locks the PDA. A Reflashing Module immediately grants the basic lead for its rank without a minigame or additional traces. A Master PDA guarantees a legendary stash. Nitro can restore the PDA to working order for a fee, after which it must be hacked normally. 

%c[255,255,190,90]3. Traders and characters%c[default] 
Hawaiian sells coordinates for: 

%c[255,130,220,120]• green stash — 500 RU;%c[default] 
%c[255,100,205,235]• cyan stash — 3,000 RU;%c[default] 
%c[255,190,140,230]• purple stash — 8,500 RU.%c[default] 

No more than five leads can be bought per in-game day: up to three green, two cyan, and one purple. Hawaiian does not sell red coordinates. 

The Keeper grants a red lead for one of these cooked-artefact sets: 5 modificats, 3 mesomodificats, 2 hypermodificats, or 1 Absolute. 

%c[255,255,190,90]4. Strange consumables%c[default] 
Strange Stew, Strange Vodka, and Strange Drink cause a blackout and attempt to move the player 14–16 meters from a purple stash. No marker is granted; the stash must be found normally. 

Different events may follow the move. Stew triggers an attack by weak mercenaries, Vodka may leave a well-equipped zombified corpse nearby, and the Drink randomly chooses one of those branches. Vodka or the Drink can also produce no additional event. 

%c[255,255,190,90]5. PDA applications and coordinate notes%c[default]
Winning a PDA application on Normal or Hard difficulty grants one lead. Easy difficulty gives no reward. The tier is fixed for that game; reloading cannot reroll it.

A coordinate note points to a stash containing an uncollected Ghost City or Life Before the Accident document. Story documents are not selected while either collection remains incomplete. After all 80 notes are collected, it switches to the next personal-story document, checking cyan, then purple and legendary stashes. Documents 11–12 remain cyan-only. If no suitable target is available, the note is not consumed.

%c[255,170,220,255]How to loot a stash correctly%c[default] 
A stash counts as searched when its container is opened for the first time. A new lead or note may appear then. A purple stash also checks a 6% ambush chance at that point. Legendary (9%) and red (12%) stashes check for an ambush only after the last item is removed. Reopening or moving items around does not grant another event attempt. 

The main contents are determined in advance. Reloading does not change the loot, and reopening the container does not create a fresh set of items.

If an ordinary artefact detector has not been found yet, first-find protection applies. The Echo, Bear, and Veles are guaranteed on the 6th, 11th, and 21st combined searches of purple, legendary, and red stashes. The Svarog is guaranteed on the 7th search of legendary and red stashes only. These counters run in parallel. Reopening and reloading do not add searches; an earlier find closes that model's guarantee. 

After the last item is removed, the container and its marker disappear. Once the player moves far enough away, the freed stash eventually receives a new location and new contents. 

Leaving even one item keeps the stash at its current location. 

%c[255,120,210,120]In short: inspect interiors and vehicles, keep the appropriate detector active, hack the PDAs you find, and completely empty discovered containers.%c[default]
